newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha flat amid slow physical demand.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha flat amid slow physical demand.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were little changed on Monday as slow regional demand offset mild gains on overseas crude oil markets on Friday, traders said.
"Some sellers raised their offer prices, prompted by Friday's crude gains. But they just couldn't find any buyers at the levels," one trader said.
Sluggish prompt demand kept near-term naphtha spreads in contango, with second-half August/second-half September traded at minus $3.00.
Petrochemical end-users remained laid back with their August and September requirements mostly satisfied.
Some naphtha brokers said some trading house traders were unsure of crude direction and reluctant to take firm positions.

Bids for second-half October open-spec naphtha were heard at $211.00 per tonne, against offers at $212.00, little changed from late Friday levels. The half-month spread between the first and second half of October remained unchanged from last week at minus 50 cents.
In fuel oil trading, demand from Japanese power firms was shifting from low sulphur crude back to low sulphur waxy residue as LSWR prices on a FOB Singapore basis have peaked out, traders said.
